stories.headline: Nscale's IPO filings show ByteDance was ~75% of its 2025 sales, renting Nvidia B200s in Norway

key_facts.fact: A ByteDance subsidiary in Singapore, Spring (SG) Pte Ltd, accounted for 73% of Nscale's $33M revenue in 2025 (about $24M), but ByteDance is not named anywhere in the 192-page S-1.
key_facts.excerpt: The Chinese company accounted for 73 percent of Nscale's $33 million in revenue in 2025, but it isn't named anywhere in the 192-page S-1 filing. Only an appendix mentions its Singapore subsidiary, Spring.

key_facts.fact: Spring rented 2,304 Nvidia B200 chips at Nscale's data center in Glomfjord, Norway, under a contract signed in May 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: This contract allowed Spring to access 2,304 Nvidia B200 chips at Nscale's Glomfjord, Norway, data center.

key_facts.fact: The FT reported the arrangement was legal: US export controls bar shipping the most advanced Nvidia chips to China but do not stop Chinese firms from renting them in data centers abroad.
key_facts.excerpt: The FT reported that the arrangement is legal. US export controls bar shipments of the most advanced Nvidia chips to China. They did not stop Chinese companies from renting them in data centres abroad.

key_facts.fact: The contract backed a $105M Macquarie loan which, with $35M of equity, paid for the chips; Macquarie required Nscale to monitor and report 'compute anomalies or suspicious configurations' that could breach export controls.
key_facts.excerpt: Macquarie compelled Nscale to monitor how the Chinese subsidiary used the AI chips and report "compute anomalies or suspicious configurations" that might be in violation of the U.S.'s export controls.

key_facts.fact: Nscale, backed by Nvidia, is reportedly seeking a valuation of up to $35B in its US IPO; the prospectus was filed with the SEC on 18 September and leaves offering size and price blank.
key_facts.excerpt: The FT has reported that the company is seeking a valuation of up to $35bn. The prospectus still leaves the offering size and price blank.

key_facts.fact: Nscale has since signed compute deals worth up to $44B with Microsoft and $45B with Anthropic, and says its largest customer will fall below 20% of revenue this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale expects its largest customer's share to drop below 20 percent of revenue this year and keep shrinking as its big contracts with Microsoft and Anthropic grow.

stories.headline: China surveys Broadcom switches in state data centers, finding up to 90% share

key_facts.fact: China's State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC) has spent recent weeks surveying how extensively Broadcom switches are deployed across state-controlled data centers, the FT reported on 23 September.
key_facts.excerpt: The State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC), which oversees state-owned enterprises, has spent recent weeks surveying how extensively Broadcom's switches are deployed across state-controlled data centres

key_facts.fact: The survey found Broadcom switches could account for as much as 90% of the equipment in use.
key_facts.excerpt: The survey found that Broadcom switches could account for as much as 90% of the equipment in use, the report added.

key_facts.fact: SASAC may issue informal guidance telling state-run data centers to scale back Broadcom switches under Beijing's 'domestic chips for domestic use' campaign.
key_facts.excerpt: SASAC may issue informal guidance directing state-run data centres to scale back their use of Broadcom switches as part of Beijing's "domestic chips for domestic use" campaign

key_facts.fact: Nvidia products have already been barred from state-backed data centers; Broadcom, Nvidia and Huawei all sell high-end switches in China.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom, along with Nvidia and China's Huawei, sells high-end switches within the country. Although Nvidia products have already been barred from state-backed data centres, Broadcom's switches remain widely present

key_facts.fact: The inquiry also examines whether Broadcom used its market position to force bundling or bulk-purchase requirements, limiting Chinese network-equipment makers such as H3C and Ruijie.
key_facts.excerpt: simultaneously investigating whether Broadcom exploits its market position through forced bundling or bulk chip purchasing requirements. The inquiry also examines how such practices limit Chinese network equipment makers like H3C and Ruijie

stories.headline: Anthropic in talks to lease up to 1 GW directly from Apollo-owned Stream Data Centers

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is in early talks to lease up to 1 gigawatt of compute capacity from Stream Data Centers, majority-owned by Apollo Global Management, according to The Information.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is in early-stage talks to lease up to 1 gigawatt of computing capacity from Stream Data Centers, a move that would significantly scale up its infrastructure ... according to a report from The Information

key_facts.fact: Anthropic would become a direct tenant of Stream's sites rather than routing the capacity through Amazon or Google.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is negotiating a direct lease for up to 1 gigawatt of compute capacity from Stream Data Centers rather than routing the deal through Amazon or Google, its two primary cloud partners

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is likely to equip the facilities with TPUs co-designed by Broadcom and Google, though Nvidia GPUs or other chips remain possible.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is likely to equip the facilities with tensor processing units (TPUs) co-designed by Broadcom and Alphabet's Google. However, the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) from Nvidia or other specialized AI chips also remains a possibility.

key_facts.fact: Talks have included the possibility of Google providing a credit guarantee for the project.
key_facts.excerpt: The talks have also included the potential for Google to provide a credit guarantee for the project, The Information reported.

key_facts.fact: Developers estimate a 1 GW compute footprint needs at least $40B of capital investment; nothing has been signed.
key_facts.excerpt: Developers estimate that a one-gigawatt compute footprint requires at least $40 billion in capital investment ... Nothing is signed.

stories.headline: Qualcomm unveils Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Extreme Gen 6, its first 2nm chips, at 5GHz

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm introduced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 at its Snapdragon Summit in Maui on 22 September.
key_facts.excerpt: Sep 22, 2026 MAUI ... Qualcomm introduces Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6

key_facts.fact: Both are built on a 2nm process — Qualcomm's first 2nm silicon — with two prime cores up to 5GHz and six performance cores up to 4GHz.
key_facts.excerpt: Both Gen 6 chips are built on a 2nm process ... with two big cores at up to 5GHz and six performance cores running at up to 4GHz. ... The two 8 Elite Gen 6 chips are Qualcomm's first 2nm silicon

key_facts.fact: The Adreno GPU is 35% faster than the previous generation, and the NPU is 14% faster with 20% better performance-per-watt.
key_facts.excerpt: an Adreno GPU that's 35 percent faster than the previous generation ... the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6's NPU is 14 percent faster and offers 20 percent better performance-per-watt

key_facts.fact: The Extreme version can run AI models with more than 30 billion parameters on-device and records 8K video at 60fps.
key_facts.excerpt: including that ability to run AI models with more than 30 billion parameters ... better video recording that tops out at 8K at 60fps

key_facts.fact: Motorola's Signature 27 is the first phone confirmed to use the Extreme chip; Xiaomi, OnePlus, Oppo, Vivo, Honor and others will adopt the platforms.
key_facts.excerpt: Motorola is the first to jump on board, confirming that its newly announced Signature 27 flagship will use the Extreme chip.

stories.headline: Chinese foundry CanSemi prices Shenzhen IPO to raise up to $918.5M; Alibaba Cloud a backer

key_facts.fact: CanSemi Technology is seeking to raise 6.16 billion yuan ($918.5M) in a Shenzhen listing after pricing shares at 12.01 yuan, a filing showed on 23 September.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese chipmaker CanSemi Technology is seeking to raise 6.16 billion yuan ($918.5 million) in a Shenzhen listing after pricing its shares at 12.01 yuan each

key_facts.fact: Gross proceeds rise to 7.08 billion yuan if the overallotment is fully exercised; strategic investors including an Alibaba Cloud unit, Goodix and Biwin Storage take half the shares.
key_facts.excerpt: gross proceeds will rise to 7.08 billion yuan. Strategic investors will take half of the shares on offer. They include Hangzhou Alibaba Cloud Feitian Information Technology, Shenzhen Goodix Technology and Biwin Storage Technology.

key_facts.fact: Subscriptions open on 24 September; if listed, CanSemi would be the first wafer foundry on the ChiNext board.
key_facts.excerpt: will begin its IPO subscription on Thursday ... if the listing is completed, the company will become the first wafer manufacturer to be listed on the ChiNext board

key_facts.fact: CanSemi runs two 12-inch fabs with 80,000 wafers/month planned capacity (63,300 reached by end-2025) and is building a third line of 40,000 wafers/month.
key_facts.excerpt: CanSemi currently operates two 12-inch wafer fabs, with a combined planned capacity of 80,000 wafers a month. By the end of 2025 the capacity had reached 63,300 wafers a month.

key_facts.fact: Revenue grew from 1.04 billion yuan in 2023 to 2.58 billion yuan in 2025, while net losses widened to 2.35 billion yuan; the company says it could turn a profit as early as 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: CanSemi's revenue was 1.04 billion yuan in 2023, 1.68 billion yuan in 2024 and 2.58 billion yuan in 2025 ... net losses of 1.92 billion yuan, 2.25 billion yuan and 2.35 billion yuan ... could turn a profit as early as 2029.

stories.headline: Alibaba Cloud to open first regions in Turkey, Finland and the Netherlands within a year

key_facts.fact: At its Apsara Conference on 23 September, Alibaba Cloud said it will establish its first cloud regions in Türkiye, Finland and the Netherlands over the next 12 months.
key_facts.excerpt: Over the next 12 months, Alibaba Cloud will establish its first cloud regions in Türkiye, Finland and the Netherlands

key_facts.fact: It will also expand data center capacity in Malaysia, Germany, the UAE, France and Hong Kong; it currently runs 107 availability zones in 31 regions.
key_facts.excerpt: while expanding its data center footprint in Malaysia, Germany, the United Arab Emirates, France and Hong Kong ... The cloud leader currently operates 107 availability zones in 31 regions around the world.

key_facts.fact: The Netherlands data center is the first to open, in October, CTO Li Feifei said.
key_facts.excerpt: The first of these new data centres will open in the Netherlands in October ... said Li Feifei, the CTO and president of international business at Alibaba Cloud

key_facts.fact: Alibaba has not disclosed site capacity, capital spending or accelerator configurations for the new regions.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba has not disclosed site-level capacity, regional capital spending, accelerator configurations, or which AI services will be available at launch.

stories.headline: Pew: 54% of Americans now say data centers are bad for the environment, up from 39% in January

key_facts.fact: 54% of US adults say data centers are mostly bad for the environment, up from 39% in January 2026; 50% say they are bad for home energy costs, up from 38%.
key_facts.excerpt: More than half of Americans (54%) now say data centers are mostly bad for the environment, up from 39% in January. Half say they are mostly bad for home energy costs, up from 38%.

key_facts.fact: 49% say data centers are mostly bad for quality of life nearby (up from 30%); only 4% see a mostly good impact in each of those areas.
key_facts.excerpt: And 49% say they are mostly bad for people's quality of life nearby, up from 30%. ... Just 4% of Americans think data centers have a mostly good impact in each of these areas.

key_facts.fact: A majority of Americans say they would be uncomfortable with a new data center operating in their area.
key_facts.excerpt: A majority of Americans would be uncomfortable with a new local data center

key_facts.fact: The survey of 10,548 US adults was conducted July 20 to Aug. 9, 2026, amid spreading protests against new data center construction.
key_facts.excerpt: The survey comes as protests against new data center construction have spread ... The new survey was conducted from July 20 to Aug. 9 among 10,548 U.S. adults.

sources.title: Americans' views of data centers have turned more negative
